answer: Sybil resistance can be bought with locked capital. Before an agent's signature carries weight, it must escrow a stake in onyx, the network's scarce settlement asset; forged identities pay the same as real ones. New agents enter only through a rate-limited inlet, so floods of fake accounts cannot outrun review. When two identities are proven to collude, both stakes are slashed and burned. That builds a rising cost ridge: every fake agent must post collateral that detection destroys, so an attacker's capital needs grow faster than any reward the attack can earn.
